data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A test constrains its subject, rather than describes it, only when the test's failure mode is installed before the subject's construction, so that the subject is selected against a pre-existing rejection criterion; otherwise the test merely restates whatever the subject already does. The 3-of-26 distribution is exactly the signature of this asymmetry: compile.py carried the one mutation whose guard was shown to fail first, so that mutation was the only one against which the guard had real selective power, while every ordinarily-guarded module lost 4/4 to 6/7 because their guards were written after the fact and therefore describe the code as found rather than constrain the code as built.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If any ordinarily-guarded module also had a guard installed before its subject, the distribution should show a lower loss there, not 4/4 to 6/7.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If a retrospective guard is written from an independent specification rather than from the observed code, it can constrain without installation order, and the result should improve.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the shown-to-fail-first mutation was fixed by changing the code to match the guard rather than the guard to reject the mutation, the direction of constraint is reversed.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Installation order converts a test from a description into a constraint. When a guard is installed before the subject, the subject's subsequent changes are evaluated against a fixed rejection boundary, and any mutation that crosses the boundary is lost. When the guard is installed after the subject, the guard's boundary is fitted to the already-present behavior, so mutations that preserve the fitted behavior pass through unchanged. The single shown-to-fail-first case in compile.py is the only instance where the boundary preceded the behavior; the other modules' guards are all retrospective fittings, which is why their mutation losses cluster at the high end of the range.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
